title: Backend Engineer Capability Profile
description: Career lens from Fresher to Lead. Levels describe expected outcomes and depth, not intrinsic difficulty of a knowledge node.

levels.title: Fresher
levels.outcome: Can implement small changes with guidance and explain foundational concepts.

requirements.outcome: Use basic collections and explain simple trade-offs.
Recognize obvious performance differences.
Read and write basic PHP safely.
Implement routing, validation and CRUD with guidance.
Use common methods and status codes correctly.
Follow an existing request/response contract.
Understand table, key and relation basics.
Write basic SELECT, JOIN and aggregate queries.
Use the project database and migrations.
Run the development environment.
Understand why checks run before deployment.
Respond to review feedback and explain changes.

levels.title: Junior
levels.outcome: Can deliver bounded backend features independently inside an existing architecture.

requirements.outcome: Design small classes with clear responsibilities.
Implement production code and handle common language pitfalls.
Build feature slices using framework conventions.
Design a bounded endpoint contract.
Return consistent, actionable errors.
Implement an existing authentication approach.
Apply role or policy checks correctly.
Write non-trivial queries and verify results.
Place a business operation inside a correct transaction boundary.
Recognize when an index may help.
Publish and consume a background job safely.
Handle transient failure without blind retry.
Add structured logs for debugging.
Debug containerized local services.
Fix common pipeline failures.

levels.title: Middle
levels.outcome: Can own a production feature from design through operation and diagnose common failures.

requirements.outcome: Choose reasonable module and service boundaries.
Evolve contracts without breaking consumers.
Choose a practical compatibility strategy.
Design retry-safe write operations.
Model consistency boundaries across a feature.
Diagnose common concurrency anomalies.
Design composite indexes for real query patterns.
Read plans and locate common bottlenecks.
Improve query performance using evidence.
Design consumers for at-least-once delivery.
Operate and recover failed messages.
Choose cache keys and invalidation rules.
Use logs, metrics and traces to debug a feature.
Contribute effectively during incidents.
Avoid common credential and permission mistakes.
Break work into reviewable production slices.

levels.title: Senior
levels.outcome: Can design and evolve production systems, lead diagnosis and raise engineering standards.

requirements.outcome: Turn non-functional needs into design constraints.
Explain decisions in context and alternatives.
Design data flow, failure handling and operational model.
Capture consequential technical decisions.
Plan safe migration paths and incremental change.
Set API standards across multiple consumers.
Design correctness under retries and partial failure.
Diagnose database behavior under concurrency.
Diagnose complex query plans in production.
Choose and implement reliable event publication.
Design user and system behavior during convergence.
Define service objectives and error budgets.
Design useful telemetry before incidents happen.
Lead mitigation, recovery and learning.
Prioritize debt using business and operational risk.
Raise correctness and design quality through review.
Grow junior and middle engineers through feedback.
Surface and reduce delivery and architecture risk.

levels.title: Lead
levels.outcome: Can align architecture, product and team capability across a portfolio of work.

requirements.outcome: Set explicit architecture fitness criteria.
Guide boundaries across teams and products.
Facilitate high-stakes decisions with stakeholders.
Create a durable decision system, not isolated documents.
Sequence platform and product evolution.
Review and teach system design across the team.
Run evidence-based technical operating reviews.
Maintain a visible risk portfolio and intervention plan.
Shape initiatives into learning and delivery milestones.
Define role expectations using outcomes and evidence.
Build repeatable mentoring systems.
Coach engineers toward independent judgment.
Distribute ownership with clear boundaries.
Evaluate whether knowledge can be applied and taught.
Connect technical investment to user and business problems.
Measure impact beyond shipped output.
Balance product, reliability, people and platform investments.
Contribute technical leverage to product strategy.
